newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks fall on election result but no panic.
newsitem.headline: French stocks fall on election result but no panic.

text.p: The Paris bourse's blue chip index fell on Monday after the left won Sunday's parliamentary election, but not as sharply as anticipated, as investors took a wait-and-see approach.
After opening 2.76 percent lower, the CAC-40 blue chip index was down 35.20 percent, or 1.36 percent, at 2,548.74 at 1025 GMT. The CAC-40 June futures contract was down 44 points at 2,523.
Volume was a heavy five billion francs.

Although the result showed the Communists will hold the balance of power in a Socialist-dominated left-wing majority in the National Assembly, the least attractive scenario for the markets, investors are staying cool.

"People aren't that scared," one trader said. "They can't raise taxes. The right already did that. They can make life miserable for companies trying to restructure but they can't stop that. They'll do symbolic things."
Caution is expected to prevail, however, ahead of the full impact this afternoon of foreign investor reaction.

The performance varied by sector, with stocks involved in privatisations and restructurings suffering far more than the market as a whole. In contrast, shares in dollar earners, consumer goods companies and retailers outperformed.
Lagardere was down 6.7 percent on concern the Thomson-CSF privatisation would be halted. Thomson-CSF shares were down 7.6 percent.
Dassault Aviation, which risks being nationalised if the privatisation of its merger partner Aerospatiale is scuppered, was suspended limit-down.
Financial and auto shares were also weak on concerns that restructurings involving redundancies might be delayed.

Shares in pen and lighter maker Bic were up 2.35 percent and food group Eridania Beghin-Say added 2.1 percent. Exporters and dollar earners also fared better than the market as a whole, with oil company Elf Aquitaine up 3.99 percent.
